name: Seorim
overview: Seorim was a male Levite who served as the fourth priest chosen among the twenty-four courses established for temple service. He belonged to the lineage of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron through whom the priestly divisions were organized. His role highlights the structured priestly order in ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Seorim means 'one born at the time of the barley harvest,' reflecting a connection to the agricultural cycle in Israel. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:8 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Seorim is identified as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to the priestly lineage descending from Aaron's son. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional family details for Seorim.
scriptureSignificance: Seorim's significance lies in his appointment as the fourth priestly leader among the twenty-four divisions that organized temple worship during the time of King David. His inclusion in the Ithamar line emphasizes the continuity of priestly duties through Aaron's descendants, ensuring orderly service in the sanctuary. This structured division was vital for maintaining the worship practices prescribed by God to Israel.
